QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_42

question.text: Over-claiming of impact is a common SIA challenge. Which techniques are recommended in Section 5.12 to mitigate it?

answer.text: Assigning roles to intervening variables, capturing quality-of-life indicators by stakeholders, and using dead weights
Compounding all beneficiary responses regardless of overlap
Ignoring intervening variables to keep the report simple
Only counting direct, un-triangulated beneficiary testimony

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook p.135 (Section 5.12) states that over-claiming can be avoided by assigning roles to intervening variables, capturing quality-of-life indicators by stakeholders, and using dead weights. Option A repeats those three techniques. The Trap: B is the classic over-claim mistake (double counting). C removes a standard remedy. D actively amplifies over-claim by relying solely on un-triangulated testimony. Note: The three mitigation techniques on p.135 are the operative source-backed list; cite them directly when explaining the answer.
